To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
urea crosses the membrane by passive diffusion when the cell is supplied with an excess of nitrogen.
urea uptake in Corynebacteria is a secondary transport system catalyzed by an inducible urea permease and that urea uptake and urea hydrolysis are independent processes.
Corynebacterum glutamicum has an inducible urea uptake system that catalyzes the active transport of urea against a concentration gradient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of urea in Corynebacterial cells.
the regulation of urea uptake and urease expression in C. glutamicum.
the characterization of the uptake and catabolic systems of urea in Corynebacterial glutamicum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

urea is taken up by C. glutamicum by two different mechanisms: by diffusion when urea is present in the growth medium in sufficient amounts and by an energy-dependent uptake system when the nitrogen supply is limited.
the urea transport system is not the rate-limiting factor for growth with urea, but rather urease activity.

the urea uptake and the urease activity in C. glutamicum are of minor importance for the nitrogen economy of this bacterium, since the urea concentration in the environment is usually low and the urea concentration inside the cells is high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Corynebacterum glutamicum is able to utilize urea as a nitrogen source.
urease is the main enzyme for the catabolism of urea, but that urease activity is not the rate-limiting step for the utilization of urea as a nitrogen source.
urea is taken up by C. glutamicum via two mechanisms: passive diffusion and carrier-mediated transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
urea uptake in Corynebacteria is mediated by a secondary transporter, the activity of which depends on the nitrogen source.
the urease system in C. glutamicum is not a major player in the assimilation of urea.
the expression of urease is not required for the growth of Corynebacterum glutamicum on urea.
